title: Legacy features
description: The original T&K2 features, including exploration, colonies, magic and automation.
text: Home / T&K2 / Legacy features T&K2 archive Legacy features The original T&K2 features, including exploration, colonies, magic and automation. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . ► Exploration Exploration in this modpack is a thrilling and diverse experience, enhanced by a combination of biome expansion, dungeon crawling, and an overhauled endgame. Biome Expansion The world generation is enriched by the inclusion of Biomes O' Plenty and Oh The Biomes You'll Go . These mods introduce a vast array of new biomes, each with unique landscapes, flora, and fauna. Whether you're traversing mystical forests, arid deserts, or vibrant meadows, these biomes add depth and variety to every exploration adventure. Caves The underground adventure is greatly enhanced with Alex's Caves , which introduces five new cave types that add complexity and interest to the mining experience. These new cave types make underground exploration more engaging and diverse. For more details, you can visit the Alex's Caves Wiki . Dungeons For adventurers seeking danger and treasure, the modpack includes both When Dungeons Arise and Integrated Dungeons and Structures . When Dungeons Arise adds massive, sprawling dungeons that challenge even the most seasoned players. These dungeons are filled with tough enemies, intricate layouts, and abundant rewards, offering a grand adventure for those brave enough to enter. Integrated Dungeons and Structures creates dungeons that seamlessly integrate with other mods like Create , Quark , Alex's Mobs , and Supplementaries . These dungeons are designed with complex machinery, unique mob encounters, and rich detail, making them a vital part of the exploration experience. Endgame Overhaul The journey to the End is no longer just about finding a stronghold and activating the portal. With End Remastered , the process becomes a grand adventure of its own. The End portal now requires 15 unique Eyes of Ender, each obtained through quests and challenges spread across the world. This change turns the quest for the End into a true test of exploration and endurance. Paired with Integrated Stronghold , the stronghold itself has been completely overhauled. The stronghold now features enhancements from mods like Create , Alex's Mobs , Quark , and Mowzie's Mobs . Expect intricate machinery, enhanced mob encounters, and the presence of powerful foes like the Wroughtnaut from Mowzie's Mobs. This makes the journey to the End not only longer but far more rewarding and challenging, culminating in a battle-ready stronghold that's as dangerous as it is awe-inspiring. ► Building Building in this modpack is a dream come true for creative players, offering a vast array of blocks and decorative options that cater to every architectural style. Modern Furniture MrCrayfish's Furniture Mod: Refurbished brings a modern touch to your builds with a wide range of contemporary furniture pieces, perfect for creating sleek, stylish interiors. Fantasy and Medieval Furniture Handcrafted adds a collection of fantasy and medieval-style furniture, providing the perfect accents for castles, fortresses, and rustic homes. Small Decorative Blocks Beautify offers small decorative blocks that add the finishing touches to your builds, enhancing the atmosphere of any space. Industrial and Mechanical Decor Create Deco integrates seamlessly with the Create mod, adding beautifully crafted, industrial-style decoration blocks that complement any mechanical build. Expanded Building Blocks Chipped dramatically expands your building palette with a plethora of new block variations, allowing for more detailed and creative designs. Natural Building Materials In addition to these mods, the world generation mods Better End , Better Nether , Oh The Biomes You'll Go (BYG) , Biomes O' Plenty (BOP) , and Regions Unexplored provide an extensive range of natural blocks and building materials, further expanding your creative possibilities. Summary Whether you're constructing a cozy cottage, a grand castle, or a futuristic factory, this modpack offers everything you need to bring your architectural visions to life. ► Mobs Mobs are made more diverse and interesting with mods like Alex's Mobs and Mowzie's Mobs , which introduce a wide range of new creatures with unique behaviors and abilities. Ice and Fire: Dragons adds mythical beasts that bring both challenge and reward. These mods together create a dynamic and unpredictable world where every encounter can be thrilling and dangerous. ► Quests The modpack comes with an extensive quest system, featuring over 1400 quests spread across 11 progression-based tabs, Exploration Tabs and More!. These quests cover various aspects of gameplay, including exploration, magic, technology, and more. The quests are designed to guide players through the modpack's content, providing rewards and goals that enhance the overall experience. ► MineColonies MineColonies is a key component of this modpack, giving players the tools to create and manage their own colonies. This mod allows you to recruit citizens, assign jobs, and build infrastructure, transforming a small settlement into a bustling town. The strategic elements of managing resources, expanding your colony, and defending against threats add depth and replayability to the gameplay. ► Magic Magic in this modpack is a rich and varied experience, offering players multiple paths to explore the mystical arts. Whether you prefer the structured spellcasting of Ars Nouveau , the dark, ritualistic power of Malum , the natural harmony of Botania , or the classic spellcraft of Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks , there's something here for every aspiring mage. Ars Nouveau lets you craft your own spells from the ground up, giving you the freedom to create magical solutions tailored to your needs. Whether you're conjuring fireballs, healing allies, or automating your base with magical constructs, Ars Nouveau provides the tools to turn your imagination into reality. For those who crave the darker side of magic, Malum offers a deep dive into the world of rituals and soul manipulation. Harness the power of the spirits, perform complex rituals, and unlock abilities that blur the line between life and death. Malum's magic is not for the faint of heart, but for those willing to embrace the shadows, it offers unparalleled power. Botania , on the other hand, is all about the synergy between magic and nature. This mod allows you to tap into the natural world to generate mana, which can then be used to craft powerful tools, gear, and gadgets. From creating beautiful, functional gardens to wielding mana-infused weapons, Botania makes you feel like a true nature mage. Finally, Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks adds a classic touch to the magical lineup. With wands, spellbooks, and a wide variety of spells to learn and master, this mod brings a more traditional magic experience into the mix. Whether you're summoning familiars, casting elemental spells, or teleporting across the world, Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks will make you feel like you're attending your own personal wizarding school. With these powerful mods at your disposal, magic becomes a central element of your journey through the world, offering endless possibilities for creativity, power, and discovery. ► Combat The Epic Fight mod transforms Minecraft's combat system into a more dynamic and visually engaging experience, reminiscent of action RPGs. This mod replaces the standard combat mechanics with a system that emphasizes timing, movement, and weapon variety, making every battle feel more intense and strategic. How It Works Epic Fight overhauls the way combat functions in Minecraft by introducing new animations, attack styles, and a dedicated combat mode. When combat mode is active, your character will perform different actions based on the type of weapon you're wielding, whether it’s a sword, axe, or even bare fists. Key Features Combat Mode Toggle (R) : To switch between building and combat modes, simply press the R key. In combat mode, your character's movement and actions change to fit the more dynamic combat system. For instance, sprinting becomes a dodge roll, and standard attacks become combos and power strikes. Weapon-Specific Animations : Each weapon type comes with its own set of animations and attack patterns. For example, wielding a sword allows you to perform quick slashes, while an axe delivers slower but more powerful strikes. The mod also supports shields, bows, and other weapons, each with its own unique combat style. Weapon Types The Epic Fight mod supports a wide variety of weapon types, each with unique animations and combat styles. The available weapon types in the modpack include: Swords Katanas Tachis Spears Battlestaffs Daggers Axes Greatswords Shields Tridents Bows Crossbows Mod Integration and Custom Support This modpack comes with full custom support for Epic Fight, seamlessly integrating it with every weapon in the game. In addition to vanilla weapons, the modpack specifically supports weapons from the following mods: Simply Swords Knaves' Needs L'Ender's Cataclysm The Aether Twilight Forest Deeper & Darker Applied Energistics 2 (AE2) Better Nether Better End Farmer's Delight Ice & Fire: Dragons Alex's Caves Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks Botania Ars Nouveau Malum Mowzie's Mobs ► The Skill Tree The Passive Skilltree Mod in this modpack introduces a deep and customizable skill tree, inspired by the complex and rewarding systems found in games like Path of Exile. This mod allows players to tailor their character's abilities to fit their preferred playstyle. To gain skill points, the modpack features a custom-made item called the Skill Point Scroll . These scrolls can be obtained randomly through quests, adding an element of surprise and reward as you progress. Additionally, defeating bosses guarantees a Skill Point Scroll drop, ensuring that your most challenging victories are always rewarded with a chance to further enhance your character's capabilities. If you ever want to reset your skill tree, the modpack also includes a custom-made Reset Scroll . This scroll can also be obtained through questing, providing flexibility and allowing you to reallocate your skill points as you see fit. To access the skill tree, simply press the "O" key, and you'll be able to navigate the extensive array of skills available. With over 300 different skill points to choose from, the Passive Skilltree Mod allows for a highly personalized and strategic approach to character development, making every choice and point allocation meaningful. ► Automation Automation in this modpack is a central theme, driven by the incredible versatility of the Create mod. The entire progression system is built around 11 tiers of custom recipes, meticulously designed to integrate Create with other major mods like Thermal Expansion , Applied Energistics 2 , and more. Thanks to KubeJS , over 500 custom recipes have been crafted to ensure a seamless integration of Create with these mods, enhancing your automation capabilities at every tier. As you progress, you’ll unlock increasingly complex machines and automation setups, making use of different Create addons like Create Crafts & Additions and The Factory Must Grow (TFMG) . The Factory Must Grow (TFMG) adds new layers to the automation process by introducing oil and advanced steel production mechanics, further expanding the industrial capabilities of your setups. These additions allow for more complex production chains and higher-level machinery, making automation more intricate and rewarding. From basic contraptions to intricate production lines, the possibilities are nearly endless. By the time you reach the final tiers, you’ll be able to automate almost everything in the game, from resource gathering and processing to complex crafting sequences. Whether you're looking to streamline your mining operations or automate the production of high-tech machinery, this modpack's automation system provides all the tools you need to turn your factory dreams into reality. title: A New World · legacy update
description: The original 1.20.1 update and its eleven-chapter direction.
text: Home / T&K2 / A New World · legacy update T&K2 archive A New World · legacy update The original 1.20.1 update and its eleven-chapter direction. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . 1.20.1 "A New World" Update The 1.20.1 "A New World" update marks a complete rework of the modpack, evolving from its previous 1.18.2 version to introduce a wealth of new content and improvements. This ambitious update has been over a year in the making, expanding the modpack from its original 7 chapters to 11 chapters of progression, offering players more depth, challenges, and rewards as they journey through the modded world. Major Changes and Additions 500 Recipe Changes : The update includes a comprehensive overhaul of the crafting system, with around 500 recipes being reworked to better integrate with the new and existing mods. This ensures a more cohesive and balanced gameplay experience that enhances the progression and crafting aspects of the modpack. 1400 New Quests : To guide players through the expanded content, 1400 new quests have been added. These quests are designed to not only introduce the new features and mods but also provide a structured progression that keeps the gameplay engaging and rewarding from start to finish. New Mods and Removals : As part of the rework, several mods have been removed to improve stability and performance, while many new mods have been added to bring fresh features and fun to the modpack. This careful curation of mods ensures that the pack is more streamlined and enjoyable than ever before. Major Mod Changes The 1.20.1 "A New World" update brings significant changes to the mod lineup, ensuring the pack remains streamlined, balanced, and fully compatible with the latest Minecraft version. Here are some of the key changes: Removed Mods : Industrial Foregoing : Removed as it didn't fit the theme of the pack and wasn't a good addition overall. Immersive Engineering & Immersive Petroleum : These mods have been replaced by Create: The Factory Must Grow , which aligns better with the modpack's focus and provides a more cohesive experience. Buzzier Bees, Autumnity, Atmospheric : These mods were removed due to their unavailability on 1.20.1. Beyond Earth : Replaced with Ad Astra , offering a more refined space exploration experience. Blood Magic : Removed as it no longer fits within the theme and balance of the modpack. Hex Casting : Also removed due to thematic inconsistencies. Blue Skies : Replaced with the Aether Mod , which better suits the overall feel of the pack. Backpacked, Functional Storage, Iron Chests : These storage mods have been replaced by Sophisticated Backpacks & Storage , offering a more unified and feature-rich storage solution. Tinkers' Construct : Unfortunately, due to a lack of updates for 1.20.1, Tinkers' Construct has been removed from the pack. Psi : Removed for the same reason as Tinkers' Construct, due to it not being updated for 1.20.1. Pam's HarvestCraft : Removed due to outdated textures and features that no longer align with the visual and functional standards of the modpack. Added Mods : Let's Do Mod Series : This series has been added to introduce new crops, blocks, and features like wine making, brewing beer, and much more, enriching the farming and crafting aspects of the modpack. Apotheosis : Reintroduced with significant nerfs to ensure a balanced and enjoyable experience that fits within the modpack's progression. Simply Swords : Hundreds of new weapons have been added, with Knaves' Needs providing compatibility for mods like Twilight Forest, BetterEnd, and Better Nether, expanding combat options. Iron's Spells & Spellbooks : This new magic mod allows players to create spellbooks with unique spells for both utility and combat, offering a fresh magical experience. Alex's Caves : Adds massive caves with unique biomes and mobs, enhancing the underground exploration aspect of the game. Passive Skilltree : This mod introduces a skill tree system with over 300 different skill points, allowing players to build their own unique playstyle. Choose from Armorer skills for increased durability or Hunter skills for more damage, among many other options. Improved Stability and Features With the "A New World" update, players can expect not only more content but also a smoother, more stable experience. The update has been optimized to reduce crashes and improve overall performance, making it easier to dive into the complex world of mods without interruptions. Ongoing Support The 1.20.1 update also marks the beginning of more active updates and patches. The modpack will receive regular support, ensuring that bugs are promptly addressed, new features are added, and the community’s feedback is incorporated into future updates. title: Legacy server installation
description: The original server instructions. Check the legacy pack and platform before following them.
text: Home / T&K2 / Legacy server installation T&K2 archive Legacy server installation The original server instructions. Check the legacy pack and platform before following them. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . You need Java 21 to host 1.20.1 modpacks. Download the Serverpack Navigate to the Curseforge page for the version you wish to play. Go to the Files tab and click the latest file. Navigate to Additional Files and download the serverpack files. Running Your Server Before anything, make sure you've extracted the initial serverpack file you downloaded! Windows If you see a startserver.bat file in the serverpack, double-click it to run your server. macOS Open the Terminal app (found in /Applications/Utilities/ ). Type cd <path_to_installer> and press Enter to navigate to the installation folder. Replace <path_to_installer> with the actual path. If you don't know the path, type cd (with a space) and drag the installer folder into the Terminal. Run the following commands: chmod +x ./startserver.sh (this makes the script executable). ./startserver.sh (to run the installation script). Linux Ensure curl is installed (if using Ubuntu, you may need to install wget to get curl ). Navigate to the modpack directory and make the script executable: chmod +x startserver.sh Start the modpack with: ./startserver.sh Common Questions How do I join my server? Install the modpack using a modded launcher (e.g., Curseforge, ATLauncher). Go to the Multiplayer tab in Minecraft. Click Direct Connect and type localhost . How do others join my server? They will connect using your Public IP Address. Find it by typing "my ip address" in Google. If they can't join, look up a port forwarding guide online. How do I allocate more RAM? Open the user_jvm_args.txt file. Cahge the Java arguments within the quotation marks. For example, -Xmx8g will set maximum RAM usage to 8GB. Should I be worried about errors in the console? Unless something isn't working as expected, most errors (99%) mean nothing important. Why is my server so laggy? Follow this guide for optimal Java arguments (note: these can cause instability for some users). If lag persists, use this in-game command: /spark profiler start --only-ticks-over 50 . Check the Spark Profiler link in chat/console and verify if your server is using all available memory. You can allocate more memory or check resource usage in the Spark Profiler. Ask for help in the Discord if needed. How do I make my server public? To get your server listed in the Server Browser , click the Add Server button in the Multiplayer menu. Servers hosted with Bisect get higher placement on the server list. Make sure to post under the correct modpack. Alternative to Self Hosting If you'd prefer a hosted solution, consider using Bisect for server hosting: Prices range from $10 to $25 per month (depending on the plan). Use code Mika for 25% off. We suggest choosing at least 1GB per player (minimum 4GB for server stability). You can order a plan here . title: Epic Fight combat
description: Weapon families, fighting approaches, stamina, skills and the selected combat addons.
text: Home / T&K3 / Epic Fight combat Combat & magic Epic Fight combat Weapon families, fighting approaches, stamina, skills and the selected combat addons. WEAPON CONTROL · TIMING · STAMINA Epic Fight turns equipment choices into movement and attack decisions. Learn a weapon in a safe area, then combine its reach and recovery with your class statistics. Classes & professions changes attributes; Epic Fight's combat skills are a separate system. Your first training session Check Options → Controls for combat-mode, dodge, guard and special-attack bindings. Toggle combat mode, practise an attack chain, then test how quickly you can move or defend afterwards. Repeat with the equipment you actually intend to wear. Watch stamina before committing to another attack. Armour weight affects stamina demands; impact helps overwhelm stun resistance, while armour negation changes how attacks penetrate protection. Damage alone does not describe a weapon's handling. Author gameplay guide . Choose a fighting approach These are practical playstyles, not an additional installed “Fighting Styles” mod. Approach What to practise Useful comparisons Agile melee Short commitments, repositioning and dodge timing Sword, dagger and fist weapons Heavy pressure Spacing, recovery windows and impact Greatsword and greataxe-style weapons Reach control Keep opponents near the end of your attack range Spear and polearm families Technical defence Timing a block and preserving stamina Guard-compatible swords and katana families Spellblade Alternate casts with safe melee openings Iron Spells integration plus a compatible weapon Ranged support Maintain distance and a route to retreat Ranger attributes and ranged equipment A class does not force an Epic Fight weapon family. Match its actual bonuses and penalties to your equipment rather than assuming a subclass name changes animation or combo rules. Weapon families The core compendium covers swords, axes, longswords, greatswords, spears, daggers, fists/gloves, tachi, uchigatana and bokken. Two items with the same family can still have different attributes. Addon weapons may use bespoke animations and skills. Family Starting question Author reference Greatsword Can I finish the attack before the enemy retaliates? Greatsword Longsword Which stance and defensive skill fit this encounter? Longsword Spear Where should I stand to use my reach? Spear Tachi When can I safely commit and when should I defend? Tachi Combat skills Slot / skill Purpose Compatibility notes Roll / Step Dodge and reposition Stamina cost is affected by equipment weight Guard Block supported attacks Sword, axe, longsword, greatsword, spear, tachi, uchigatana Parrying Timed defence Requires Guard; sword, longsword, tachi, uchigatana Impact Guard More resilient blocking Requires Guard; spear, longsword, tachi, greatsword Passive skills Alter stamina economy or combat attributes Examples: Technician, Berserker, Sword Master, Stamina Pillager Mobility / revelation Special movement and encounter tools Examples: Demolition Leap, Phantom Ascent, Meteor Slam, Revelation Skill-book access and numerical bonuses depend on the installed release and configuration. Read the current skill tooltip before selecting it. Epic Fight's Berserker skill and T&K's Berserker subclass are distinct choices. Author skill reference . The alpha's combat addons Weapons of Miracles supplies distinctive weapons and associated skills. The author's examples include Agony, Torment, Ruine, Antitheus, Satsujin, Herrscher, Moonless and Solar, alongside staffs, a greataxe and Ender Blaster. Practise each weapon's own mechanics; the project description is not an alpha loot table. Author project . The alpha also lists Simply Swords , Integrated Simply Swords , Iron Spells X Epic Fight , Enhanced Animations , Ice and Fire X Epic Fight , Epic Fight: Curios Compat 2.0 , Epic ParCool , ParCool and Minecolonies: Epicfied . These connect equipment, casting, movement or entities to combat. Inclusion does not prove that every third-party weapon has a correct moveset; check it in combat mode. Troubleshooting & preparation A weapon uses an unexpected animation: check its Epic Fight capability/compatibility patch rather than changing its name. A defence skill will not activate: check the equipped skill, required predecessor, weapon family and stamina. Spellcasting feels different in combat mode: inspect both Iron Spells and Epic Fight bindings, then test the selected integration. Heavy armour leaves little room to dodge: compare a lighter loadout before adding more damage. Before a boss, test a full attack–defend–retreat cycle. Bring a fallback weapon, food and an escape route. Explore encounters · Combat magic · Accessories . title: Iron’s Spells & addons
description: Spellbooks, schools, scrolls, casting and the installed integration projects.
text: Home / T&K3 / Iron’s Spells & addons Combat & magic Iron’s Spells & addons Spellbooks, schools, scrolls, casting and the installed integration projects. FIND A SCROLL · BUILD A BOOK · CHOOSE YOUR SCHOOL Iron's Spells provides prepared spells, mana, casting equipment and school specialisation. Start with a useful scroll, equip a book and learn its range and casting time. Search the spell catalogue for the documented base and addon definitions. Scroll to spellbook A scroll can cast a spell consumably or be inscribed into a spellbook at the Inscription Table . The Scroll Forge uses paper, ink and a school focus to make scrolls; the Arcane Anvil supports spell and equipment upgrades, including eligible weapon imbuing. Check JEI and the item tooltip for the exact installed recipe and restrictions. Author overview . Choose a book with appropriate spell capacity, then equip it as instructed by its tooltip. Check Controls for selecting and casting spells. Try your spell away from a settlement before relying on it in combat. Schools & identities This table follows the author's school reference for the documented 1.21-era system. Newer wiki material can differ from the alpha's release. School Identity School focus in the reference Fire Fire-based attacks Blaze Rod Ice Ice and freezing effects Frozen Bone Lightning Electrical attacks Bottle of Lightning Holy Healing and holy magic Divine Pearl Ender Teleportation and spatial magic Ender Pearl Blood Blood-themed offence and sustain Blood Vial Evocation Conjured attacks and summons Emerald Nature Nature and poison magic Poisonous Potato Eldritch Restricted eldritch knowledge Echo Shard Eldritch spells require learning the relevant manuscript before use. Addons can introduce other schools; the catalogue keeps their school names separate. Author school reference . Build a useful loadout Reserve a slot for an attack you can reliably aim, then add a defensive or movement tool. A continuous cast keeps you committed longer than an instant cast. Test range, line of sight, recovery and mana consumption against ordinary enemies first. Firebolt , Heal , Teleport , Summon Vex and Black Hole illustrate different roles in the upstream spell definitions; inspect the installed spell before choosing a level or assuming access. Search their names in the catalogue. The catalogue intentionally avoids treating upstream damage and mana numbers as pack balance. Mana capacity, regeneration, spell power and school power are different statistics. The skilltree guide shows exactly which attributes each class path modifies. It does not create a separate Iron school tree. Installed spell-content addons Alpha project What to explore Documentation coverage Cataclysm: Spellbooks Cataclysm-themed spells and additional magic schools The catalogue indexes 57 definitions from the author's published 1.21.1 reference release Spellbooks of Twilight Twilight-themed spells, gear and spellbooks 22 source definitions are indexed; a source definition is not proof of alpha availability Echoing Magic Echo/cosmic spells and equipment All seven referenced spells below are indexed GTBC's Geomancy Plus Geomancy and associated spell content See author documentation; version-specific completeness is not established Alex's Caves: Spellbooks Cave-themed spellcasting equipment and summon content The author describes two summon spells; a verified full name registry is not included The Cataclysm reference release is 1.1.14-1.21 . It is a research source, not a claim about the alpha's installed jar. Each catalogue entry links its author source. Echoing Magic The referenced spells are Echo Star , Echo Blast , Echoing Explosion , Echoing Slam , Collapse , Summon Brave and Conjure Grimoray . The author documents Geomancy Plus integration for Collapse and Summon Brave; their school can change when that integration is present. Both projects appear in the alpha selection. Inspect the installed tooltip to confirm the active school. Author project . Integration & equipment projects Ars 'n Spells offers configurable connections between the two magic systems. Its documented modes include Iron-primary, Ars-primary, hybrid and separate mana behaviour. Which mode the alpha uses has not been checked from configuration; do not assume an Ars mana bonus always modifies Iron mana. Author integration guide . Create: Wizardry connects the factory to Iron's materials and processing. Iron's Gems 'n Jewelry adds its own equipment progression. Apotheosis x Iron's Spellbooks Compat , Iron's Spells x Aeronautics Compat and the Epic Fight integrations are also selected. Use the alpha list for their exact project links, and the recipe workshop for authored T&K recipes. KubeJS Iron's Spells, GTBC's Spell Lib, Ace Spell Utils and Iron's Lib are integration or support projects, rather than promises of additional player spell schools. When a spell does not work Check the book slot, mana, cooldown, learned manuscript requirements and target conditions. Confirm that the spell exists in your installed release. If an addon school differs from this reference, trust its current tooltip and configuration. Author progression guide . title: Ars Nouveau spellcraft
description: Build glyph chains, generate Source and automate with helpers and selected addons.
text: Home / T&K3 / Ars Nouveau spellcraft Combat & magic Ars Nouveau spellcraft Build glyph chains, generate Source and automate with helpers and selected addons. DESIGN YOUR SPELL · GROW SOURCE · BUILD LIVING AUTOMATION Ars Nouveau lets you assemble spells instead of only selecting predefined ones. Its personal mana powers your casting; Source supports magical machines and automation. Keep those resources distinct while learning the system. Browse the core glyph catalogue . First spell Obtain the starter spellbook using the recipe available in JEI. Open its spell editor, select a method, add an effect and save the spell in a slot. Learn more glyphs with the Scribe's Table and the ingredients shown in the installed guide. Higher book tiers unlock more advanced spellcraft. Author casting guide . Begin with one effect you can understand. Test it on a safe target before adding complexity, especially for block-changing or area spells. Understand the chain Part Job Example Method Determines how the spell reaches its target Touch, Projectile, Self or Underfoot Effect Performs the operation Break, Harm, Heal, Light or Launch Augment Modifies a compatible effect Amplify, AOE, Pierce or Extend Time Augments modify the appropriate preceding effect; they are not independent attacks. A glyph's tier, compatibility and cost influence which chains you can build. The glyph catalogue shows the compatible augments explicitly found in the referenced source, with author links for inherited behaviour. Author glyph introduction . Useful experiments These are simple core-glyph combinations to try once their glyphs are unlocked. They are learning examples rather than the strongest build or a guaranteed starting-book unlock. Spell idea Chain to test What to observe Mining tool Touch → Break Harvest level, tool restrictions and mana cost Ranged attack Projectile → Harm Travel time, aim and line of sight Personal recovery Self → Heal Healing gained compared with mana consumed Local lighting Touch → Light Target surface and placement Movement Self → Launch Height, landing safety and surroundings Add Amplify to an effect that supports it, then compare the result and cost. Add area or duration only after the basic spell behaves as expected. Avoid building a long chain whose effects compete with one another. Author spellcraft guide . Mana and Source Personal mana limits how often you cast. Source is collected by Sourcelinks and held in Source Jars , then moved through Source Relays to nearby consumers. Build a small generator, a jar and one consumer before making a large network. Check range, relay targeting and storage before assuming a machine is broken. Author Source guide . Machines & magical helpers System Role First thing to check Imbuement Chamber Magical material preparation Correct ingredients and Source conditions Enchanting Apparatus Higher magical crafting Pedestal setup and the installed recipe Starbuncle Item transport Assigned routes and valid inventory access Whirlisprig Plant-related automation Its supported environment and instructions Drygmy Creature-related resource gathering Required nearby creatures and Source Wixie Crafting/brewing automation Recipe instructions and available supplies Bookwyrm / Storage Lectern Magical storage access Linked storage and interaction setup Spell Turret Repeated spell operation Valid spell, targeting and Source supply Start each helper as a small standalone system. Add buffers between collection and processing, then connect it to Create or digital storage. The installed book is the authority for exact ranges and setup details. Author automation guide . The alpha's Ars addons Ars Creo and Create: Ars Nouveau Compat link Ars and Create systems. Ars Sable documents improved Starbuncle pathing, Source interactions across sublevels/world boundaries and sublevel warp/render support. Its presence does not guarantee every contraption has been tested. Ars Sable author project . Ars 'n Spells connects Ars and Iron's magic through configurable integration. Verify the active mode before treating both mana pools, regeneration or equipment bonuses as interchangeable. Integration reference . Reliquified Ars Nouveau adds relic-based progression around Ars mechanics; see Artifacts & Relics . KubeJS Ars Nouveau enables scripted integrations. The wider Ars guide includes many optional addons: this wiki only treats projects in the alpha list as selected. T&K workshop connection The existing campaign guide connects Ars to chapter 4 Arcane Industry , with the Enchanting Apparatus, Arcane Mechanism and Arcane Machine route. Native Source collection and authored factory recipes are separate concerns. Follow the actual recipe workshop for T&K ingredients rather than copying an upstream crafting recipe. Troubleshooting Spell will not save: check glyph tier, chain structure and augment compatibility. Spell casts but does little: check targeting, harvest level or affected entity/block conditions. Machine stops: check Source, relay connections and output capacity. Helper is idle: inspect its task assignment, environment and reachable inventory. Core glyphs · Iron’s spells · Automation . title: Witchery
description: Begin Just Another Witchery Remake: ovens, altar, brewing, rituals and advanced paths.
text: Home / T&K3 / Witchery Combat & magic Witchery Begin Just Another Witchery Remake: ovens, altar, brewing, rituals and advanced paths. NATURE · BREWING · RITUALS · TRANSFORMATIONS The alpha selects Just Another Witchery Remake , not the original 1.7.10 Witchery. Use its own Modonomicon guide and JEI recipes. This page follows the author's published 0.5.12.1 book as a reference; the alpha mod list does not identify the installed jar version. Author release . A practical beginning Open the mod's guidebook and begin with its General category. Build the preparation stations before attempting an advanced rite. Collect plant materials, reserve room around your altar and keep separate storage for essences and brewing ingredients. Station / system Purpose Starting check Oven Processes natural ingredients into essences Supply Clay Jars to capture fumes Altar Supplies power to nearby magical systems Surround it with appropriate natural variety Cauldron Brewing and magical crafting Fill with water and ignite it as the guide instructs Distillery Separates mixtures into components Follow the current recipe rather than assuming old Witchery recipes Ritual chalk Establishes ritual layouts Use the chalk and pattern named by the rite These summaries follow separate entries in the author's reference book. Exact fuel, range, capacity, recipe order and power requirements should come from the installed guide. Altar power The altar is a resource source, not a universal recipe shortcut. The reference book associates nearby nature, including trees and flowers, with increased altar power. Place your magical workspace within the required range, then compare available power with the operation's demand. If an operation fails, check both the altar's power and the rest of its conditions. Adding more power does not replace a missing ingredient, weather requirement or ritual participant. Brewing Use the Brewing book category for effect ingredients and preparation. Prepare a single recipe with a clear goal, record its ingredient order and test the result. A nearby altar may be necessary for stronger cauldron work. The reference Cauldron entry describes Wood Ash as a way to clear it before preparing another brew. The topic index contains the 34 Brewing topics in the reference release. It links your question to the right book section without substituting guessed quantities or legacy potion recipes. Rituals & the brazier The reference book contains separate Ritual and Brazier categories. Before beginning a rite, check its chalk layout, offerings, altar demand, time/weather and participant requirements. Do not assume those conditions are optional because the ingredients look correct. The author's public data-format documentation describes ordered ritual requirements and optional conditions such as altar power and coven count. That format describes what a recipe can require; each actual rite supplies its own values. Author ritual-format reference . Covens, bindings and poppets A Coven Contract organises participating players and witches in the reference book; recruitment can require fulfilling a witch's request. Keep track of the contract because destroying it disbands its coven in that release. Poppets use Taglocks to bind to a player or creature. Read whether the particular poppet must be carried or can be placed in the world. Binding, placement and target identity all matter; a generic “poppet buff” description is insufficient. Search all 223 topics and then follow the installed book's prerequisites. Version boundaries The author's 0.5 update moved soul magic and lichdom into Forbidden Magic . That addon does not appear in the supplied alpha list, so this wiki does not present lichdom as an installed alpha path. Older Witchery guides and newer addon demonstrations may describe content outside this pack. Author project and update notes . Some transformation features depend on server configuration. For example, the reference book makes spreading lycanthropy to other players conditional on the server permitting it. Inspect that setting before promising a shared progression route. Troubleshooting Check the recipe's installed version, ingredient order, heat/water state, altar range and power, target binding and environmental conditions. For an advanced path, check its book prerequisites rather than skipping directly to a final ritual. Witchery topic index · Alpha mod list · Other magic systems . title: Artifacts & Relics
description: Understand exploration accessories, relic progression and Reliquified integrations.
text: Home / T&K3 / Artifacts & Relics Combat & magic Artifacts & Relics Understand exploration accessories, relic progression and Reliquified integrations. EXPLORE · EQUIP · DEVELOP YOUR ACCESSORIES The alpha combines Artifacts, Relics and several Reliquified integrations. Start by identifying which mod owns an item, then read its current tooltip. Similar-looking accessories can follow different progression rules. Browse 74 referenced core item names . Artifacts: exploration rewards Artifacts introduces treasure accessories found through exploration rather than ordinary crafting. The author's acquisition routes include structures, archaeology, some equipped creatures and underground campsites with Mimics. A Mimic encounter can supply an artifact in the mod's default behaviour; pack loot changes may differ. Artifacts author project . Equip an accessory in the appropriate Curios slot and test its effect. Some effects are passive, while others require a condition or binding. Slots, stacking and drop chances should be checked in the installed release rather than inferred from a name. Author wiki . Relics: an item that grows with you Relics adds equipment with individual statistics, abilities and progression. Inspect an item's ability panel, development requirements and available upgrades before investing resources. Two copies need not have identical starting properties. Relics author project . Evaluate an accessory by its role: movement, defence, resource gathering, utility or damage. Check whether an ability needs a keybind, a trigger, a target or accumulated resources. Read the item-specific instructions instead of assuming all relics share an experience trigger. Why the integrations matter Selected project What changes Which reference to trust Reliquified Artifacts Adapts Artifacts items to Relics progression; some mechanics change substantially Installed enhanced item panel, not only the base Artifacts description Reliquified Ars Nouveau Adds relic progression connected to Ars mechanics Addon tooltip plus Ars guide Reliquified Twilight Forest Adds Twilight-themed boss relics Addon tooltip and the relevant boss/loot reference Artifarts Adds humorous Curios cushion content Its own item tooltip; it is a separate project from Artifacts Author references: Reliquified Artifacts , Reliquified Ars Nouveau , Reliquified Twilight Forest , Artifarts . Compare your loadout Goal Compare Common mistake Survive close combat Defensive triggers, sustain and movement Counting an effect that only activates under a condition Cast reliably Magic-related abilities and resource interactions Assuming an Ars bonus always increases Iron mana Explore safely Travel, fall protection and escape tools Testing a new effect for the first time above a fatal drop Gather resources Loot conditions and supported targets Assuming a gathering bonus affects every machine-produced item Cooperate Shared utility and your combat role Filling slots with overlapping effects that do not stack Use a safe test: equip one item, record what triggers it, then compare with your previous loadout. Combine it with class statistics and combat skills after understanding the accessory itself. Finding an item The accessory catalogue indexes core Artifacts and Relics language entries from pinned 1.21.1 source branches. It includes registry IDs and author-source links. It is a name reference, not a claim that every item is a random alpha drop or that all addon items are indexed. JEI, the installed relic panel and the author's item documentation provide the current recipe, effect and development requirements. Relics item documentation may describe a newer release; compare it with the installed tooltip. Workshop plan · Kinetic Machine
text: Follow the workshop plan and prepare this tier’s production line. Start with the manual Kinetic Machine. It gives you the powered equipment needed to automate mechanisms. This first tier needs no previous milestone. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Algal Blend
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Kelp + clay makes two blend by hand, four in a mixer. Start a kelp farm beside your workshop. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Andesite Alloy
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Andesite + blend makes two alloy by hand, four in a mixer. Original nugget alloy recipes are excluded. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Build the first frame
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Craft 7 alloy + slab + Andesite Casing in AAA / ACA / ASA. Cut separate frames into power, press, mixer and Deployer. This route needs no mechanism. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Turn the wheel
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Craft a Water Wheel from one Kinetic Machine, two Andesite Alloy, planks and a Large Cogwheel. Connect shafts and gears; supply water. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Assemble the workshop
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Use a separate manual Kinetic Machine for each starter machine. Craft the Press first, then the Mixer, Basin and Deployer with their listed parts. Keep two Deployers for alloys and a third holding the ordinary hammer. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Kinetic Mechanism
text: Complete the Kinetic Mechanism assembly in the exact listed order. Assemble one Kinetic Mechanism through its complete ordered sequence. Each material application consumes one item; the last Deployer holds the finishing tool. One full loop gives one guaranteed mechanism. Start with Wooden Slabs. Deploy Andesite Alloy. Deploy Andesite Alloy. Finish with Iron Hammer in the last Deployer. Repeated ingredients are separate ordered applications. Feed them individually, then extract the finished mechanism into a buffer.

title: Kinetic Machine
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Functional machines also require their listed working parts. Stonecutting is reserved for the listed passive fittings. Put Andesite Casing on the belt or depot. Deploy Kinetic Mechanism onto it. Follow the machine’s exact recipe: frame plus working parts. Use stonecutting only for listed passive fittings. Each machine consumes its own frame and the listed parts. Stock Alloy, sheets, shafts and tools for the complete workshop.

title: Run the workshop continuously
text: Build and test the setup described below. Demonstrate a complete material → mechanism → casing/frame → machine line. Set filters, buffers and output handling; confirm it runs without manual ingredient insertion. Stock the raw-material buffers. Run material → mechanism → casing/frame → machine. Test repeated batches and output collection without hand-feeding. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Complete chapter 1
text: Complete this chapter and claim your permanent workshop tool. Claim your unbreakable workshop tool. Completing this chapter unlocks the next tier for the team, including offline players when they next join. Claim your own reward manually. The tool is awarded once per player, even on a shared team.

title: Farmer’s Delight
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Use cutting and cooking for food. Feed wheat, kelp and bone meal to the industrial crop lines. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Chipped & Architect’s Palette
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Decorative workbenches and palette blocks are building choices. They do not substitute for progression frames. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Collect items early
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. A Hopper Upgrade pulls from and pushes to adjacent inventories. Use the Pickup Upgrade for loose dropped items; check its own range and filters. Keep wheat, kelp and clay buffers near the first workshop. Build several manual frames before automating mechanisms.

title: Workshop plan · Hydraulic Machine
text: Follow the workshop plan and prepare this tier’s production line. Follow this chapter’s material and machine path. The previous milestone unlocks this tier. Optional quests introduce supporting systems; milestone rewards grant one unbreakable tool per player. Separate water, crop supplies and sealing ingredients. Keep enough prismarine for the aquatic workshop.

title: Cure the rubber
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Compact slime, dried kelp and 250 mB water. Mix one wheat, one kelp and 250 mB water into two slimeballs; supply the seals line. Separate water, crop supplies and sealing ingredients. Keep enough prismarine for the aquatic workshop.

title: Ocean metallurgy
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Mix bone meal, kelp and water into calcium powder. Compact prismarine shard, copper sheet and powder into two alloy; rods supply the Conduit Cage. Separate water, crop supplies and sealing ingredients. Keep enough prismarine for the aquatic workshop.

Feed them individually, then extract the finished mechanism into a buffer.

title: Bootstrap steel
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Heated mixing uses two iron ingots and coal for two steel. Five steel, two osmium and one Precision Machine produce Steel Casing; no FE or boss core is required. Bootstrap with Precision Machines and heated steel before requesting Inductive or Arcane equipment.

title: First powered processing
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Deploy a Precision Mechanism onto Steel Casing. Add Heat Generator and basic universal cables. Native infusing supplies circuits and alloys. Bootstrap with Precision Machines and heated steel before requesting Inductive or Arcane equipment.

title: Charge certus
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Craft from Steel Casing, certus and Crafts & Additions Capacitor. Use FE to charge certus; native water conversion produces fluix crystals. Bootstrap with Precision Machines and heated steel before requesting Inductive or Arcane equipment.

title: Print the processors
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Steel Casing + Electric Motor + gold. All four press recipes are available from this chapter; use the normal Inscriber routes. Bootstrap with Precision Machines and heated steel before requesting Inductive or Arcane equipment.

title: Build a parallel arcane workshop
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Precision Machine bootstraps the apparatus. Bootstrap the Agronomic Sourcelink from wheat, Source Gems, a Source Jar and a Precision Machine. Make Arcane Casing and the sequenced Arcane Mechanism, then deploy the mechanism. Magic supports the factory alongside FE. Bootstrap with Precision Machines and heated steel before requesting Inductive or Arcane equipment.

title: Grow the chemical feedstock

First PRCs, separators and chemical buffers use Ender Machines; finish the native HDPE chain before expanding.

title: Forge Shadow Steel

title: Reinforced Mechanism

Deploy Shadow Steel Sheet. Deploy Hdpe Sheet. Deploy Hdpe Sheet. Deploy Elite Control Circuit. Deploy Ingot Steel. Finish with Steel Paxel in the last Deployer. Repeated ingredients are separate ordered applications. Feed them individually, then extract the finished mechanism into a buffer.

Stock Alloy, sheets, shafts and tools for the complete workshop.

title: Useful settlement details
text: Complete the detected item or boss goal below. Supplementaries and Amendments supply practical building and interaction tools. Waystones support travel alongside airships and quantum links. Keep all five core catalysts and test the complete input chain before scaling Sovereign production.

title: Your kingdom starts here
text: Find your main progression route and the supporting guides. Engineering, magic, exploration and settlement building share one adventure. Chapters I–X are the production spine. The other categories are guides and optional projects you can revisit at any time. Read this welcome page. Find the six category headings in the chapter sidebar. Open Chapter I and locate its workshop plan. Open Mechanical Quests when you want the next machine; open Character Paths when choosing your build.

title: Reading the quest board
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Round item nodes detect an item in your inventory. Guide checkmarks mean you have read the explanation; activity checkmarks mean you have completed the described setup. Large gold milestones unlock the next workshop tier. Reading guides is safe for the whole team. You can compare all classes without selecting them.

title: Claim your workshop rewards
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Item goals do not consume your materials. Each chapter milestone awards its named unbreakable finishing tool once per player. Rewards use manual claiming, so revisit completed milestones and collect your own tool. Open a completed milestone. Click its reward to claim it. Store your workshop tools separately from adventuring gear. Put the reward tool into the finishing Deployer; stock replaceable tools while you are still building the chapter.

title: Teams and personal choices
text: Understand this part of your adventure. The campaign uses FTB team quest progress. Workshop stages synchronize with completed milestones when a teammate next logs in. Your skilltree class, subclass and profession investments remain personal. Agree on who handles crops, processing and exploration, then share the finished supplies.

title: Set up your controls
text: Complete the project described below. Several mods add controls for quests, the map, parkour, combat and the skilltree. Open Minecraft Controls and search each mod name. Resolve conflicting keybinds before testing combat or a new movement ability. Check FTB Quests and map controls. Check Epic Fight, ParCool and spell controls. Check the skilltree shortcut. Search Passive Skill Tree for the class tree. The supplied tree notes O as its intended shortcut, but your actual keybind may differ.

title: Read the actual recipe
text: Complete the project described below. Use JEI to look up an item’s recipe and uses, then check every process tab. This pack changes important machine and mechanism recipes. Item names alone do not tell you which frame or processing method is required. Look up Algal Blend. Compare its manual and mixing routes. Look up the uses of a Kinetic Machine. JEI bookmarks make a useful shopping list. Keep the casing, mechanism and finishing tool together in your plan.

title: Learn a machine with Ponder
text: Complete the project described below. Supported Create items have in-game Ponder scenes for placement, rotation and interactions. Follow the tooltip’s Ponder shortcut. Use JEI for the pack’s exact ingredients and the recipe workshop on the official wiki for assembly order. Inspect a Deployer tooltip. Open its available Ponder scene. Compare the machine explanation with its T&K3 recipe. Ponder explains the machine; the T&K3 recipe entry tells you what this pack requires.

title: Read the block in front of you
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Jade supplies block and entity information when available. Tooltips, machine screens and recipe viewers together help identify a stalled process: wrong ingredient, missing power, wrong side or an unavailable tier. Check the destination inventory first when a belt stops moving.

title: Mark home and protect it
text: Complete the project described below. Use the selected map and FTB Chunks tools to mark home, claim your workshop and review team permissions. Claims, loading limits and server permissions depend on the instance settings. Create a home waypoint. Review your team’s claim permissions. Keep a clear route to the workshop. Name waypoints for farms, portals and unfinished projects, not just your main house.

title: Know the workshop gates
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Andesite starts the factory; Copper adds fields and fluids; Brass opens the Nether. Chapter IV adds AE2 and Mekanism. Chapter V opens End progression. Chemistry, expeditions, containment, quantum industry and the Sovereign project follow. A side guide may show a future project. Its TIER label and dependency indicate when you can complete it.

title: A board full of useful symbols
text: Understand this part of your adventure. The supplied quest and information artwork is used as navigation art throughout this book. Books introduce guides, maps mark expeditions, job icons mark professions and large milestone nodes mark chapter completion. Quest/info icons are reading aids. They are not ingredients or items you must craft for progression.

title: Choose a place to begin
text: Complete the project described below. Look for access to water, space for crops and a level workshop footprint. Leave room for belts, tanks, a stone generator and later machine rooms rather than fitting every process into your bedroom. Set up shelter and a bed. Mark a workshop area. Reserve a separate storage corner. A workshop next to the farm shortens the first wheat and kelp supply routes.

title: Keep your expedition fed
text: Complete the project described below. Build a steady food supply before traveling far. Farmer’s Delight and the selected cooking mods offer useful meal choices. Check a meal’s tooltip and available ingredients before planning mass production. Carry one reliable food stack and reserve special meals for longer trips.

title: The first industrial crops
text: Complete the project described below. Wheat and kelp serve both food and machine progression. Clay feeds Algal Blend, and limestone processing can supply bone meal. Keep seeds and replanting stock out of the factory’s consumption buffer. Plant wheat. Start a kelp patch in water. Reserve a chest for crops and seeds. A small reliable farm is more useful than a large farm with nowhere for its harvest to go.

title: Handcraft the starting frame
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Chapter I deliberately starts before automated mechanisms. Seven Andesite Alloy, a wooden slab and Andesite Casing craft the first Kinetic Machine. Use the manual route to obtain the machines that will automate the mechanisms. Make Algal Blend and Andesite Alloy. Craft the manual Kinetic Machine. Craft the required starter machines with their frames and matching parts. Budget several starting frames plus machine parts. The first Press uses an Iron Block; later plate recipes need that Press.

title: Give every process an output
text: Complete the project described below. A chest, hopper or an appropriate collection upgrade turns a working machine into a useful supply line. Decide where items arrive and what should happen when that inventory fills. Hopper Upgrades transfer to adjacent inventories. Pickup Upgrades collect dropped items; these are different jobs.

title: A working first workshop
text: Complete the project described below. Finish a compact area with water power, a press, a mixer and deployers. Leave paths to access filters and replace tools. Continue Chapter I for the exact progression goals. Label the ingredient buffers so you can return after an expedition and understand your own factory.

title: Pick a shared project
text: Understand this part of your adventure. This board is a collection of voluntary settlement goals. Choose projects that suit your team and current tier. The checkmarks record your work; the campaign milestones remain in Mechanical Quests. Write the project owner and required supplies on signs at the construction site.

title: The town storehouse
text: Complete the project described below. Build a central room with named storage, an incoming materials area and a tools shelf. Keep personal equipment apart from community ingredients. Reserve separate shelves for unfinished mechanisms and reusable boss cores.

title: The public kitchen
text: Complete the project described below. Connect a crop store to a kitchen, prepare a repeatable meal and create an accessible food reserve for builders and adventurers. Keep seeds, animal feed and the next recipe batch in separate buffers.

title: The workshop road
text: Complete the project described below. Connect the workshop, homes and farms with a lit road. Leave clearance for carts, contraptions and future transport stations. Build the path before placing machines across the route.

title: The guild library
text: Complete the project described below. Create a place for mod guides, enchanting supplies and the team’s build notes. Give magic experiments their own work surface. Put a sign beside each area listing its main ingredients and purpose.

title: The training yard
text: Complete the project described below. Prepare a safe practice area away from villagers and factory equipment. Test weapon moves, spells and mobility before a difficult expedition. Use the selected Dummy mod for controlled equipment comparisons when its target is available.

title: The expedition locker
text: Complete the project described below. Prepare shared supplies for a trip: food, spare tools, blocks, a return plan and free loot space. Add a board for destinations and discovered structures. Keep a recovery kit at home instead of carrying every useful item into the same fight.

title: The kingdom museum
text: Complete the project described below. Display important discoveries, decorative blocks and notes about boss victories. Keep working progression catalysts in secure storage rather than using them as disposable decorations. Make a labelled display copy where possible and retain the production original.

title: Choose how you like to play
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Warrior, Ranger, Rogue, Mage, Cleric and Occultist offer different combat foundations. Read all six class pages, then make your actual choice in the personal skilltree. You can complete every reading guide here. The questbook does not lock your class choice.

title: One class, one subclass
text: Understand this part of your adventure. The supplied tree restricts you to one class root and one subclass root. Each class has three subclass options with positive bonuses and meaningful tradeoffs. Compare those tradeoffs before investing. Choose the playstyle you enjoy during ordinary fights, not only a boss damage screenshot.

title: Build the class foundation
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Each class has five mandatory inner branches with four nodes each: twenty foundation nodes. Follow the displayed prerequisite route through class mastery and the specialization gate to reach a subclass. The twenty foundation nodes are not the entire cost of reaching a subclass; approach, root and gate nodes also matter.

title: Every node is a decision
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Every native node in the supplied tree costs one point. Point availability follows the installed Passive Skill Tree settings. A quest guide does not generate extra points or create a separate profession leveling system. Read the next node’s prerequisite and tradeoff before buying it.

title: Three paths inside a subclass
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Each subclass has three independent fourteen-node paths. Follow each branch’s own learned-skill requirements. The optional synergy nodes are side destinations; they do not skip another path’s requirements. Focus on a useful path first. The all-path apex rewards completing the foundation of all three paths.

title: Read your apex carefully
text: Understand this part of your adventure. The tree permits one subclass keystone. Advanced class branches and profession investments compete for the same points, so decide whether you want a broad character or deeper specialization. Sketch a point plan with your desired subclass path and professions before spending the last available points.

title: Professions alongside combat
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Seven profession islands support Mining, Logging, Hunting, Exploration, Fishing, Farming and Crafting. The supplied tree permits up to three profession masteries and up to three focus nodes within each profession. A class does not force a profession. A Mage can farm and a Warrior can craft.

title: Match equipment to your tree
text: Understand this part of your adventure. A tree bonus only helps when its conditions and relevant attribute apply. Compare weapon type, school, casting cost, armor and movement rather than choosing equipment solely for its rarity. Use the item tooltip and the actual skill node as the final description of their effects.

title: Warrior at a glance
text: Decide whether this combat foundation suits you. Melee pressure, health and a durable frontline. Read the three specializations below, then make your personal investment in the skilltree. Reading this page does not select the class. Compare the root’s bonuses and penalties on the actual skill node.

title: Build your foundation
text: Understand this part of your adventure. Your five inner branches are Weapon Training, Battle Rhythm, Endurance, Iron Guard and Pressure. Each branch contains four mandatory foundation nodes. Complete their requirements, class mastery and the specialization gate before entering a subclass. Twenty inner foundation nodes are only part of the route; account for entry, root, mastery and gate nodes too.

title: Berserker
text: Understand the Berserker playstyle and its tradeoffs. Higher attack damage and stronger critical damage; lower maximum health and reduced healing received. These are the subclass’s starting tradeoffs and direction, not your character’s final stat totals. Compare the subclass root with your other two options. Inspect its three paths: Fury · Brutality · Blood Price. Choose and invest in the personal skilltree when you are ready. Keep a reliable food and recovery supply. Trading defense for damage makes retreat timing more important.
